- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant explained that the $t$ distribution is a probability distribution used to make inferences about the population mean when the sample size is small and/or the population standard deviation is unknown.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant described the $t$ distribution as a bell-shaped distribution similar to the standard normal distribution but with heavier tails.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant noted that the shape of the $t$ distribution depends on the degrees of freedom, which is equal to the sample size minus one.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant mentioned that the $t$ distribution is often used in hypothesis testing to test whether the sample mean is significantly different from a known or hypothesized population mean.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant stated that a $t$-test is used to calculate a test statistic, which is then compared to critical values from the $t$ distribution to determine the p-value and make a decision about the null hypothesis.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant explained that the $t$ distribution is also used in confidence interval estimation.
